concept: Reachability Analyzer scope for customer-owned Atlas PrivateLink paths
summary: Source-anchored research for Reachability Analyzer scope for customer-owned Atlas PrivateLink paths. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Analyze the client-to-endpoint direction. AWS documents VPCE_INTRA_VPC_TRAFFIC when an endpoint is treated as initiating a connection to same-VPC resources and recommends reversing that analysis; MongoDB describes Atlas private endpoint connections as one-way. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/explanation-codes.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md

When the customer path includes AWS Network Firewall, inspect unsupported-rule messages. AWS excludes domain lists, Suricata rules and rule options from its model. Classmethod’s 2023-03-29 experiment independently found HTTP/TLS rules produced different analysis outcomes from TCP rules; that historical test is not an Atlas reproduction. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/how-reachability-analyzer-works.html ; https://dev.classmethod.jp/articles/amazon-vpc-reachability-analyzer-3-networking-services

The customer endpoint is a boundary of available evidence, not a universal PrivateLink product limit: AWS supports tracing to service targets within an organization, and Serverworks independently demonstrated analysis between consumer and provider EC2 instances across a PrivateLink lab topology. That lab does not establish access to Atlas-managed resources. (medium confidence) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/03/amazon-vpc-reachability-analyzer-3-networking-services/ ; https://blog.serverworks.co.jp/privatelink-ci-explanation
Reachability Analyzer does not consider registered-target health. A customer-endpoint path result therefore cannot establish that the Atlas-side load-balancer targets are healthy. (low confidence)

For TCP analyses whose path traverses a transit-gateway route table, AWS examines only forward traffic. That modeled result cannot establish a complete return path. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

UNKNOWN_RESOURCE means the analyzer cannot describe a resource; UNKNOWN_DESTINATION means destination information is insufficient to extend the path. Treat these as analysis visibility limits rather than evidence that an Atlas service is down. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

For an Atlas PrivateLink investigation, a defensible customer-side analysis ends at the interface endpoint or its ENI: AWS supports VPC endpoints and network interfaces as destinations, while MongoDB distinguishes that interface endpoint from the Atlas-created endpoint service and load balancer. This boundary is a synthesis of the two vendors’ documentation, not an Atlas-specific test. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/how-reachability-analyzer-works.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md

Cross-account Reachability Analyzer analysis requires AWS Organizations trusted access. Management accounts can analyze organization accounts; delegated administrators can analyze other organization accounts except the management account, plus explicitly shared management-account resources. AWS describes PrivateLink target tracing within the organization. Owning an Atlas-facing endpoint therefore does not itself establish permission to inspect Atlas-owned service-side resources; provider-side access must be separately demonstrated. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/multi-account.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/03/amazon-vpc-reachability-analyzer-3-networking-services/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md

Reachability Analyzer builds a configuration model without sending packets or analyzing the data plane. An endpoint-terminated result therefore establishes only the modeled customer-side path; it supplies no observation of traffic crossing PrivateLink into the Atlas service. (medium confidence)

The documented source and destination resources must be in the same Region; supported resources must have IPv4 addresses, and a dual-stack resource is analyzed using IPv4 only. Apply these limits to the customer workload and endpoint selected for analysis. (low confidence)
